#3173. Apple Pay just got even better with four new features and more

Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it much easier to switch between different cards during the checkout flow on websites and in apps.

In the new design, you can easily swipe between cards on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to view a grid of all your available Apple Pay cards.

The design also makes it easier to see information about individual cards, including rewards, balances, pay later options, and more.

iOS 27 was released to everyone last week. You can update in the Settings app on your iPhone.

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that lets you pay with American Express rewards points.

When shopping online or in apps with an American Express card, you’ll see a new “Use Rewards” option alongside your available Membership Rewards points balance. You can apply points to cover all or part of your purchase, right in the Apple Pay checkout flow.

American Express points redeemed via Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents each. For example, this means 10,000 points can be redeemed for $70 applied towards your purchase.

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a new “Tap to Share” feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

This feature is an extension of Tap to Pay on iPhone. Apple explains:

With just a tap, customers can connect to a participating merchant’s iPhone for a more personalized and faster in-store purchase experience that allows for secure sharing of information, such as email and other contact information, shipping address, loyalty rewards information, and more.

Customers will also be able to view the items in their basket in real time so they can keep track of what they’ve purchased and ensure all sales and discounts are properly applied.

When done, shoppers can complete the checkout on their iPhone using Apple Pay.

iPhone users with select banks can manage their debit card balances directly in the Apple Pay interface. According to Apple, you’ll be able to use Apple Pay to add money to a supported debit card directly in Apple Wallet or when checking out.

This one isn’t really a new feature developed by Apple. Instead, it’s something that should’ve happened years ago finally coming to fruition. Walmart has announced that it is finally starting to roll out support for Apple Pay. Apple Pay is also rolling out to Sam’s Club as part of this initiative.

As of November, Walmart’s roll out of Apple Pay across the United States is complete.

As Apple Pay continues to increase in popularity and prevalence among retailers, it’s great to see Apple continue to improve the experience. Personally, Apple Pay is my checkout payment method of choice basically everywhere I shop — whether that’s online or in store.

#3172. This Magnetic Phone Neck Mount Was the Easy Filming Solution I Needed, and It's on Sale for Black Friday

I write a lot about e-readers and e-ink tablets for Lifehacker, and one issue I'm constantly grappling with is how to write informatively about a bunch of devices that can be quite different in some details, like build or native firmware, and pretty much identical in others, given that literally all e-ink devices use display technology produced by the same Chinese company. (It's called E-Ink.) The best way to do this is to include more video in my articles, but I've lacked a good way to film hands-free so I can easily demonstrate a device's look and feel—until recently.

I recently got an offer to try out a magnetic neck mount from Telesin, a low-cost option to turn my iPhone into a wearable so I can keep my hands free while filming. It's a pretty basic concept, but well-executed: The band that goes around your neck is made of rubber with a firm but flexible core, so you can easily position it to be longer or shorter or at an angle, and the phone mount is on an extending arm with three joints to give you additional options.

I haven't had a chance to film anything for public consumption quite yet, but my testing has already given me some great ideas for how I can use it to show off, say, what it's really like to use a micro-reader in comparison to a full-sized Kindle, as I'll be able to wear it to give a more accurate user's point of view. And right now is a good time to pick one of them up, as many of Telesin's phone and camera accessories (including similar models built to handle an action camera like a GoPro) are discounted for Black Friday; the one I tested is down to $17, or 15% off.

This won't be the right device for every filming scenario. Though MagSafe holds my iPhone fairly securely, I found that I would accidentally detach it every time I tried to adjust the shooting angle—once even leading me to drop it. That's potentially bad news, as using it may require you to take the phone out of its case if it isn't MagSafe-compatible. (Mine isn't.) But if you're just looking for an inexpensive way to shoot hands-free video in a controlled environment, it could be exactly what you need.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

#3170. Breaking Baz: ‘Bunker’ Writer-Director Florian Zeller Takes Us Behind The Scenes With Penélope Cruz, Javier Bardem, Stephen Graham & Dame Eileen Atkins

Speaking over Zoom from his home in Paris, Florian Zeller says he could write poems all about Penélope Cruz. Instead, he wrote a thrilling movie called Bunker for her, and her husband, Javier Bardem.

Zeller, the playwright, screenwriter and screen and stage director behind The Father (for which Anthony Hopkins won his second Best Actor Oscar) and plays that have run on Broadway and in London’s West End, emphasizes that he wasn’t interested in Cruz’s radiant beauty. “Of course she’s beautiful,” he says, but, “somehow we don’t care.”

What do you mean? I ask. Related Stories Trailers 'Bunker' Trailer: Penélope Cruz & Javier Bardem Clash In Florian Zeller's Venice Breakout; UK Release Date Set News Netflix Unveils Penélope Cruz & Juan Diego Botto's Domestic Violence Drama 'Patricia' As Production Gets Underway

“Of course, she is talented, but she has something more, something unique, and it has to do with the fact that she’s always working with who she is. She’s always working with her deep emotions, and that in my experience is really rare.” Watch on Deadline

We both extol the three performances Cruz appears in this season. First, his Bunker, of course, in which she plays Sofía, an accomplished editor of foreign fiction at an upscale London publishing house. Bardem plays Miguel, her husband, an eminent architect, who’s handy in the kitchen and adores preparing the family’s meals. In addition, in the Los Javis-directed La Bola Negra, Cruz plays Nené Romero, a cupletista, who performs bawdy songs for troops during the Spanish Civil War. Then in Olivia Wilde’s chamber comedy The Invite, she shows off her comedic chops in the role of Piña, one half of a couple with an experimental approach to partnership.

But it’s Bunker that gives Cruz a lead role and center stage.

As to how Zeller connected with Cruz and Bardem he explains that he had a meeting with Cruz four years ago “but the project was not the right one.” Then, one day, Bardem rang him and marveled over Zeller’s plays and films, saying that he’d screened The Father countless times to study Anthony Hopkins’s performance, to understand how he did it. A little while later, they were both in Los Angeles and Bardem visited Zeller and spent an afternoon in his LA garden “talking about life.” That’s when Zeller shared his desire to write something for both Bardem and Cruz.

Zeller says now that part of his motivation was because they are “such an iconic couple then reality would go almost against fiction, and so I thought it would be much more interesting, challenging, and beautiful to have layers to every scene and to blur the line between fiction and reality.” As with Nicole Kidman and Tom Cruise in Stanley Kubrick’s Eyes Wide Shut and Mike Nichols’s screen version of Edward Albee’s seminal play Who’s Afraid of Virginia Wolf? with Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, we’re fascinated when reality meets fiction, or vice-versa, but it’s not, as Zeller puts it, “to put ourselves in a position of voyeurism.”

(By the way, there’s a fabulous revival of Albee’s Who’s Afraid of Virginia Wolf? on now at @sohoplace Theatre in London’s West End starring Gillian Anderson and Billy Crudup directed by Marianne Elliott.)

Sofía and Miguel have been married for 16 years, just like Cruz and Bardem. The fictional couple in Bunker seem happy at first, but you sense in Sofía that there’s a growing distance. There’s a brilliant opening scene where Sofía and Miguel are dining with friends and Miguel begins to tell fellow guests the story of how they met. However, the camera’s real focus is on Cruz’s face. She’s just listening and says nothing in that moment. “You can feel everything that she is feeling,” says Zeller, “and only the greatest actress can do that with almost no words to say and to express so many things, so many layers. And that’s what I love about that scene. Her face is like a landscape. You know, looking at her to see the how intense, complex, and rich she can be in this quieter, more contained exploration of who she is — that’s something of a new journey of performance.”

Zeller observes that he and Cruz talked a lot about that opening scene, “and the fact that it was about not what she says but what she keeps for herself, and because in the film we feel that she’s going through a crisis without knowing exactly what it is. In another scene she is in front of this painting. Suddenly, she feels melancholy, but we don’t know exactly why. She’s not happy with her life without knowing exactly why…You know, she has a beautiful house, she has a beautiful husband, she has beautiful children, and still, she is unhappy. She doesn’t have the words to describe why she feels that way. What is this melancholy? So, it’s not until the moment comes when there’s this long confrontation and this long argument with Javier, when suddenly she can articulate her thoughts and her feelings. But until then, and it was the challenge for her as an actress, it was to make us understand everything that she’s going through without being able to express it.” Zeller says that “everything that matters was behind the dialogue” and that Cruz’s “silent intensity” blew him away. Me too.

Zeller continues, “You know, I’ve been lucky enough to work with so many great actors, and I can say that she’s really extraordinary to work with. She’s extraordinary, versatile, but always truthful, always intense. She’s never cheating. You know, every emotion she is exploring is coming from a true place, and I think that’s why she’s so special in this industry now…It’s really rare.”

Of Bardem, Zeller observes that he usually plays “very powerful men, very masculine, frightening sometimes, sometimes really scary, and when I met him, I was touched by the fact that he’s such a sensitive, such a delicate, and I would say, almost such a feminine man. And that’s what I wanted to explore in this film. Not to say that this is his story. Of course, that’s not his story and that’s not her story. But what I was really interested in was to try to still leave room for who they are in this film. But what you feel about this character is at least what I feel about who he is as a man, this very delicate way of seeing the world and trying always to leave room for the other. You know he has such a delicacy towards Penélope, for example, and so I feel like it’s almost them, even though it’s characters.”

It’s true that the fear is at the core of the film, and because I think that it’s one of the feelings that really defines the world we are in at the moment. It all started, as you might know, with an article that I read about this tech billionaire building a bunker.

Zeller ensured that they read the script several times “to be aware of what would be the exposure,” and calls the couple “very brave as artists.” As soon as they made the decision to do it, they expressed no fear “to be seen the way they wouldn’t want to be seen.” Their commitment,” he adds, had to do with “the trust, of course,” but also, “with the feeling of being safe. It’s true on set but it’s true in every professional situation that you are a better version of yourself when you feel safe, and as an actor, you feel safe when you feel loved. So, part of my job was to love them or to make them feel loved, and it was not that hard because I truly loved them,” he says.

I ask Zeller to talk about the film’s gripping 12-minute fight scene between the couple, that took three days to shoot. He noticed that Cruz “was really nervous about it, days and days ahead of it.” And when it came time to shoot, Cruz had to be “very mad,” so Bardem “was saying off-camera things that would make her mad.” He laughs. “Javier knew which buttons to push.” Zeller remembers Bardem telling him one day that there was no need to rehearse the couple arguing because they knew how to do that, and in any case not rehearsing that scene would save the production money, a point that Zeller, as a producer of the film, acknowledged.

In bringing Graham on board as the neighbor, Zeller says he admired the actor’s performance in Netflix hit, Adolescence, but for Bunker he was looking for an actor “that was capable of putting Bardem at risk. It’s not that easy because usually Javier Bardem is the one to threaten everybody else. And for some reason, Stephen Graham has this menacing presence.” But he was also struck by Graham’s ability “to have something so human.” It’s a small but integral part and Zeller was struck by Graham’s humility. Zeller says, “When he read the script, he said, ‘OK, it’s not a big role, but I know exactly what I can do with that. I know exactly why I want to do it.’”

“It’s not a conscious reference, because that play is not clear in my mind,” says Zeller, “but it’s true that the fear is at the core of the film, and because I think that it’s one of the feelings that really defines the world we are in at the moment. It all started, as you might know, with an article that I read about this tech billionaire building a bunker.” When I suggest that Zeller and I must’ve read the same article in the New York Times about Mark Zuckerberg and his bunker, Zeller responds, “Exactly.”

He was, he says, struck by the idea that this man “who made a fortune from the idea of connecting people together was working at the same time on a plan B to isolate himself.” That’s what gave him the impetus to write the film. “It’s such a strange position in life to have to work on something that would mean that maybe soon it’s the end of the world. The more I was thinking about it, the more I realized that, to some degree, we are all tempted to live in a bunker,” he says. He clarifies, “like an invisible bunker to build things to feel protected, without realizing that it’s another kind of prison.”

Zeller worries that we are all adopting the lifestyle “that these billionaires are promoting, it is a world of illusions where you almost believe that you don’t really need the others. You know, like everything could be delivered to you, like food, love, friendship, social interactions, cinema, as if the world out there was not a place to explore anymore. As if we were like isolated islands and not interconnected continents.”

Speaking of “interconnections,” there’s a reconnection of sorts in Bunker. Several years ago, Zeller penned the West End and Broadway play The Height of the Storm which starred Dame Eileen Atkins and theatrical knight Jonathan Pryce. During pre-production on Bunker, Zeller approached Dame Atkins to ask if she’d take a cameo role of a woman who meets Cruz’s character in a powder room and offers her some sage advice. It’s just a moment on screen, but it holds enormous symbolism, that of one great artist passing the baton to another.

Zeller nods in agreement and speaks of his “respect and admiration” for the classically-trained Atkins, now in her 93rd year. The grande dame had told Zeller that she was retired. So, while the interiors were being shot in Madrid to allow Cruz and Bardem to be close to their children, Zeller was so keen to have Atkins in his film that he offered to shoot the scene in London.

What followed was “a very moving moment” because it was the last scene shot in the film, “so it was the wrap for Penelope and for her, and it was really emotional because the scene is very short and it’s basically her saying, ‘You’re so beautiful, and you should enjoy it because you know things are going very, very fast, faster than what you think,’ which is a very simple and common thought. But that’s also the truth. Not only a character saying that to another character, but it was also a woman of a certain age saying that to Penélope, and it was also an older actress that had stopped working saying that to another actress. So, it was so many layers of transmission between two women. I mean, they both cried at the end, and then, it was so moving, Eileen said, ‘Oh, that was my very last apparition on the screen.’”

Sony Pictures Classics opens Bunker in select U.S. cities on December 11 and then nationwide on January 15, 2027.

StudioCanal will release the film in the U.K. and Ireland on February 19.

Whenever I visit my parents, we go through our family albums together and reminisce about times gone by. That's why I adore instant cameras, and I test the best of them for a living.

I highly recommend buying an instant camera if you feel the same way — and Black Friday is the best time to do so, whether you're getting one for yourself or as a gift for a loved one. I've sifted through Adorama's and Amazon's Black Friday sales and handpicked the best deals for you.

If you want a simple point-and-shoot instant camera, the 4.5-star Fujifilm Instax mini 13 is down to $79 at Adorama. It's supremely easy to use, regardless of age and expertise. For more creative control, I recommend the Fujifilm Instax mini 99 which is 23% off at Amazon right now.

Don't fancy an Instax? The Polaroid Go Gen 3 (Bundle) is available for $98 at Amazon, and it's a highly pocketable camera for travel. If you want an instant camera with autofocus and one that takes high-quality photos, the Polaroid Flip (Bundle) is $40 off at Adorama.

And there's more where that came from! Here are my top seven Black Friday instant camera deals. If you need gifting inspiration, don't forget to check out my photography gift guide.

The Fujifilm Instax mini 13 is the best value for money instant camera around. It takes lovely photos with retro colors, and its controls are so straightforward that anyone, regardless of age or experience, can use it. It comes in fun colors, too. This deal takes $10 off the camera.

The Fujifilm Instax mini LiPlay is a great hybrid instant camera and printer that lets you take retro photos but also print your own from a smartphone. It produces lovely images and lets you add filters and frames. It can also print photos with audio!

The Fujifilm Instax mini 99 is for the person who takes their instant photography seriously. Five shooting modes give you a level of creative control you simply don't get on the other models in this lineup, and six colour effect settings let you push the aesthetic of your prints in genuinely interesting directions

The Fujifilm Instax mini Evo allows you to get truly creative with 100 different effect combinations, and the images it produces are gorgeous. The camera performs fantastically in low-light conditions too, and it’s compact and portable, making it ideal for travel.

The Fujifilm Instax mini Evo Cinema is the only instant camera that, alongside being able to shoot and print stills, can also record video and add them to prints in the form of QR codes. Image and video quality is outstanding, and thanks to a new Eras or Gen Dial and Degree Control, you can apply a total of 100 effect combos to your creations.

The Polaroid Go Gen 3 is a cute little camera — in fact, it's the world's smallest instant camera, according to Polaroid! The Polaroid Flip features the brand's iconic design with modern innovations. Sonar autofocus, a hyperfocal 4-lens system, a powerful flash, scene analysis which checks for over or underexposure — there's a lot to love about the Flip. It captures lovely photos with a retro aesthetic, too, of course. This bundle includes an 8-pack of film.

Black Friday sales are here and come with some worthwhile discounts on Soundcore's Nebula projectors. Prices start at $299 for the compact Nebula P1i and go up to $2,799 for the premium X1S 4K laser projector, with savings of up to $700 across the models we've rounded up. There's quite a bit of variety here, too, from battery-powered projectors you can take camping or move between rooms to more powerful 4K models designed for a dedicated movie-night setup.

The Soundcore Nebula P1i is down to $299 from $399, while the Nebula P1 is $699.99, down from $799. Both offer 1080p resolution and Google TV, but their speaker setups are what make them interesting. The P1i has two 10W speakers that flip out and rotate to direct sound toward your seating area, while the P1's speakers detach completely and can run wirelessly for up to 20 hours. The P1 is also brighter at 650 ANSI lumens versus the P1i's 380, though you'll need a power outlet for either projector since neither has a built-in battery.

Small enough to slip into a bag, the Nebula Capsule 3 and Capsule 3 Laser are worth considering if you want something you can easily take on trips or move around the house. The standard Capsule 3 is down to $399 from $529, saving you $130, while the Laser version is $649.99, down from $749.99. Both offer 1080p resolution, automatic image adjustments, and up to 2.5 hours of battery life, although the Laser model is a little brighter at 300 ANSI lumens compared with the standard model's 200.

Taking movie night outdoors is a little easier with a battery-powered projector, and both the Nebula Mars 3 Air and Mars 3 are designed for just that. The smaller Mars 3 Air is down to $519.99 from $599.99, offering 1080p resolution, 400 ANSI lumens of brightness, and up to 2.5 hours of playback. The larger Mars 3, now $899.99 from $999.99, steps things up with 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to five hours of battery life in Eco mode, and a more powerful 40W speaker. It also has a weather-resistant design that's useful for camping or backyard screenings, though its extra bulk might make it less convenient to carry around.

If you're ready to move beyond 1080p, the Nebula Cosmos 4K SE at $1,099.99 (originally $1,299.99) offers a more affordable way to get 4K resolution. Its hybrid LED and laser light source delivers up to 1,800 ANSI lumens, while its Dolby Vision support helps bring out more detail in compatible movies and shows. You also get Google TV and automatic image adjustments for easier setup, though it doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'll need a power outlet nearby.

At the premium end of Nebula's lineup, the X1 and newer X1S are designed for a more serious home theater setup. The X1 is down to $2,299 from $2,999, saving you $700, while the X1S is $2,799 from $3,299. Both use triple-laser technology with 4K resolution, Dolby Vision, and optical zoom, but the X1S has a considerable advantage in brightness, reaching up to 6,000 ANSI lumens compared with the X1's 3,500. That extra brightness is useful in rooms with some ambient light, but the tradeoff is louder fan noise.

#3164. Aaron Rodgers Released By NFL’s Pittsburgh Steelers Following ESPN Interview Where He Criticized Coach Mike McCarthy After Benching

Aaron Rodgers has been released by the Pittsburgh Steelers following an explosive interview on ESPN‘s Pat McAfee Show.

The Super Bowl champion and 4x NFL MVP was benched this week, and backup quarterback Mason Rudolph was named to take his place in the Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos.

Rodgers, a frequent caller on the sports show, appeared to discuss the situation and, moments later, was confirmed to have been let go by the Steelers.

“I got the day off, so that’s why we’re able to do this,” Rodgers said on the ESPN talk show. Related Stories Sports NFL On The Future Of Netflix's Thanksgiving Eve Game & Starting A New Tradition: "We Are Committed" News Netflix Releases New Peter Berg-Directed Spot Inspired By 'Friday Night Lights' Highlighting Thanksgiving Eve Game

Rodgers said he heard he would be inactive for Amazon’s Prime Video game on Friday from a phone call with other members of the organization, not from Coach Mike McCarthy, whom he had spoken to earlier that day. Watch on Deadline

The football star noted that he had been talking to McCarthy in the last days, but talks about benching were not part of their conversation. Rodgers recalled his interactions with the Steelers coach in the last few days and claimed McCarthy came into a quarterback meeting “late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring.”

Rodgers said that after waking himself up again, “five minutes later, you hear the snoring again and less than five minutes after that he walks out of the room like nothing happened.” He added that McCarthy didn’t show up to other meetings and walk-throughs that week.

The quarterback said he had expressed concern over McCarthy’s health, approaching him as a friend, since sleeping during a meeting is a sign someone isn’t healthy.

Later on in the interview, Rodgers suggested that what was best for the team was for McCarthy not to call the plays anymore, adding, “If he wasn’t up for that, then they should probably release me.”

“At this point, I’m not going back to Pittsburgh. That ship has definitely sailed,” he said.

Shortly after his interview on The Pat McAfee Show, reports said Rodgers had been released.

Rodgers signed with the Steelers this season as a swan song and was planning to retire from the NFL at the end of the season. With Rodgers being released, any team can sign him until 4 p.m. ET on Thursday. If he goes unsigned, he would become a free agent.

#3163. Two billion credentials publicly exposed, including everything needed for identity theft

A security researcher has discovered a publicly exposed database containing approximately two billion credentials. The database was neither password-protected nor encrypted.

The scariest part of it is around 400,000 documents came from separate folders for individual victims, creating a detailed profile with all the personal data needed to “own that person” …

Cybersecurity researcher Jeremiah Fowler says that the database contains a huge array of information, including login details for Tor .onion addresses used to access the dark web.

I also observed thousands of Tor .onion addresses associated with account names and passwords. The Tor .onion services are generally categorized as part of the dark web, and these credentials could potentially provide access to private forums, marketplaces, communication platforms, or other hidden services. While .onion accounts alone do not imply criminal or malicious activity, it is estimated that as much as 60% of dark web sites host illegal material and illicit activities. This is the first time I have seen a large number of dark web accounts in breached credentials. It should be noted that legitimate organizations, journalists, whistleblower platforms, and news organizations also operate .onion services to provide anonymity and bypass censorship.

But the most frightening aspect of it is separate folders for individual victims containing all of the information needed for identity theft.

Fowler told Wired that this data appears to have been obtained through advanced malware.

The “scariest” thing in the database, Fowler says, was around 400,000 documents that appeared to come from “more advanced malware” compiling information about individual victims […] that create a detailed profile of an individual and their digital life. “If you had that, you own that person,” Fowler says.

There’s no information about the specific sources of the data, but it seems likely to be aggregated from a range of data breaches. Fowler contacted the hosting company to have the database removed, but it’s not known how many people may have had access to it.

The best protection is to use a password manager like Apple’s Passwords app to ensure you have strong, unique passwords for each individual website and service you use, with two-factor authentication enabled wherever possible. When given the choice of 2FA code delivery, you should always opt for an authenticator app rather than a text message to protect yourself against SIM-swap attacks.

#3162. Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed To Saturday Due To Severe Weather; NBC Will Rerun 2025 Parade On Thursday

The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed until Saturday due to expected storms on Thursday, and NBC will rerun last year’s parade this Thanksgiving.

In a statement, NBC says, “Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided, in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28.

“More details to follow,” the statement continues. “In addition, NBC will telecast the 2025 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones.” Related Stories News NBC Tracking Storm Due To Hit 100th Annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: Will Balloons Be Grounded? News Jack McBrayer To Host NBC's 'Countdown To Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade' Featuring Interviews With Leslie Odom Jr & McKenna Grace

As reported by Deadline yesterday, NBC had been closely tracking the Thanksgiving storm expected to bring high winds and heavy rain to New York City and much of the Eastern U.S. The network’s coverage of the 100th edition of the annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade was set to air Thursday on NBC and stream on Peacock from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET. Watch on Deadline

The parade remains a major draw, with last year’s pulling in 34.3 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, its biggest combined audience on record.

The Nor’easter, a classic storm pattern, is expected to take shape late Wednesday and into Thursday morning, gathering strength as it grinds toward the Atlantic Ocean later in the holiday. Sustained winds are expected to be 12-25 miles an hour with gusts of 20 to 30 mph, increasing over the course of the day. AccuWeather is expecting one to two inches of rain to fall on New York, making this likely to be one of the wettest Thanksgivings in the city’s history.

This year’s parade is especially significant to Macy’s and NBC, as it marks the broadcast’s centennial. The parade is set to have 100 of its trademark large balloons, and a special “All-Star Broadway Thanksgiving Day Celebration” will feature performers from new and long-running Broadway productions in a special 10-minute medley.

The balloons have only been grounded once before, in 1971, due to a similar mix of rain and wind.

During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, the parade was converted into a television-only event around the Herald Square location of Macy’s Department Store.

#3161. How Microcredentials Can Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

IEEE Credentialing Program pairs AI governance standards with microcredentials

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

“AI ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

For engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

The IEEE Credentialing Program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. By pairing cutting-edge AI governance standards with targeted microcredential programs, IEEE provides engineers and IT leaders with clear, standardized road maps to build systems that are not just technically advanced but also safe, compliant, and worthy of public trust.

To learn more about the credentialing program, explore the offerings or connect with an IEEE expert.

Kaitlyn Ridel is a marketing specialist for the IEEE Microcredentialing Program

#3159. TIME’s Top 100 Photos of 2026 list includes a shot taken on iPhone 18 Pro

In September, Apple held a photography exhibition in New York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera. Now, an image of the Bugaboo Mountains from that exhibit, shot by photographer Jimmy Chin, is included in TIME’s Top 100 Photos.

TIME publishes its Top 100 Photos list each year. The list showcases the pictures that the TIME Photo Department determines best capture that particular year.

The essence of TIME’s Photos of the Year, selected by our photo editors and presented below, is the authentic, sometimes staggering, reality captured by photojournalism. Someone was there. A news photographer lifted a viewfinder, pressed a button, and captured an instant happening in front of them.

Chin’s image was shot in Bugaboo Provincial Park, Canada, on iPhone 18 Pro. He explained that a traditional production creates a layer of separation between the photographer and the subject, with equipment, crew, and all the moving parts of a shoot. Shooting on iPhone 18 Pro meant that he could create a more intimate environment, allowing for a sense of comfort and spontaneity that comes through in the images.

Image Courtesy of Apple (as featured in the What Holds Us exhibition)

Chin’s goal was to capture the intersection of human ambition and the pursuit of wonder against the backdrop of a timeless natural landscape.

“The resolution and the sharpness on iPhone 18 Pro surprised me. I could shoot a few inches of rock and ice, or a massive panorama, and trust it would hold at size. That is what this work needed. It also meant I carried almost nothing. In the mountains, everything you carry is a decision. I was not thinking about gear. I was thinking about what was in front of me.”

Apple’s “What Holds Us” exhibit ran in New York City in September, featuring work from photographers Alex Prager, Jack Davison, and Jimmy Chin, with each artist using the iPhone 18 Pro to explore the “people, places, and ideas that connect and ground humanity.” Kathy Ryan, the former longtime director of photography for The New York Times Magazine, curated the exhibition.

The exhibit is now headed to London, where it will open to the public on December 4, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. It will also be open from Saturday, December 12 through Sunday, December 13, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

You can view the full list of this year’s TIME 100 Photos right here.

Apple's latest flagship smartwatch, the Apple Watch Series 12, is worth the upgrade. It's certainly one of Apple's best smartwatches, but that also means it isn't cheap: All these new features give the new Series 12 a starting price of $399, which only increases if you choose a model with cellular data. However, for Black Friday, you can take up to $100 off the Series 12, bringing the starting price down to $299.

The three biggest hardware upgrades with the Apple Watch Series 12 are the heart rate sensor, the S11 chip, and Ceramic Shield 2. That heart rate sensor now checks your pulse every five seconds, or 20 times a minute. Apple says the Series 12 checks your heart rate variability 24 times more than the Series 11, and your background heart rate 60 times more frequently than the Series 11. The company is even so bold as to say the Series 12 has the most accurate heart rate monitor on a wearable.

Powering the new heart rate monitor is the S11 chip, Apple's latest processor for the Apple Watch. The S11 isn't only responsible for these new heart rate features, however. In addition to running the same watchOS 27 features as other compatible Apple Watches, the S11 on the Series 12 can run Audio Intelligence, Apple's new suite of AI-powered audio features. That includes "Live Rewind," which lets you see a transcript of the last 15 seconds of an in-person conversation, and "Siri Recaps," which displays summaries of your conversations throughout the day. Finally, the other major advantage with the Series 12 is Ceramic Shield 2. This is a display upgrade that Apple typically reserves for more premium Apple Watch finishes, but this year, the aluminum Series 12 gets it as well. That means the watch should be more durable against scratches and cracks, without you having to upgrade to the more expensive model.

How much you'll save on a Series 12 depends on the size, color, and model. At this time, Amazon is selling certain colors of the 42mm Series 12 for $299, while certain colors of the 46mm option run $449 (also marked down by $100). You can also save on the cellular models as well: The 42mm option is currently $429 (down from $499), while the 46mm model is $449 (down from $549).

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

#3155. iPhone Handoff: Here’s the latest on carrier availability and pricing

iPhone Handoff is a new feature in iOS 27 that lets you use the same phone number across two different iPhones. However, the feature requires carrier support, so it isn’t available to everyone. Here are the carriers that currently support iPhone Handoff and those that have promised support.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Score Sony’s INZONE noise-canceling earbuds for 38% off. These deliver immersive 360 Spatial Sound, active noise canceling, low-latency wireless connectivity, and much more.

With iPhone Handoff, you can use the same phone number on two different iPhones. Your number automatically moves between the two phones, depending on which one you pick up. This includes calls, voicemail, messages, and Find My location.

Simply unlock whichever device you want to use and you’re ready to go. Other data synced with iCloud will automatically update across your devices. Third-party apps work across both devices, following each app’s own syncing behavior.

iPhone Handoff is available on iOS 27 and later. The phones must be connected to Wi-Fi, share the same Apple Account, use Messages in iCloud, and be signed into FaceTime and iMessage with the same Apple Account.

The biggest limiting factor of iPhone Handoff is that it requires carrier support. Currently, just three carriers support the feature:

What about carriers that are working on the feature? In the United States, Verizon has promised it “will support iPhone Handoff,” but it’s unclear when the feature will launch. Verizon says it will charge $10 per month for the service.

AT&T, meanwhile, has no plans to support iPhone Handoff. In a statement in September, the carrier said that its focus “remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence.” The carrier noted that there “could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff,” but that customers should use “existing eSIM activation and transfer options” instead.

No other carriers have promised support for iPhone Handoff, so it’s unclear how quickly the feature will expand around the world.

In my testing, iPhone Handoff works really well. I have it set up between my iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo. I use the iPhone Duo 90% of the time, but when I do pick up my iPhone 18 Pro, my number instantly switches to it. There’s a cute animation that expands from the Dynamic Island, confirming that the number has moved.

Have you tried iPhone Handoff? Are you willing to pay extra for it? Let us know down in the comments.
